title: Measure retrieval and check claim support
notes: 3 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Two evaluation layers answer different questions. Define: Retrieval asks whether evidence was found; grounding asks whether a claim follows. Walk through: A relevant passage can be retrieved while the answer misstates its threshold. Ask: Can perfect retrieval recall guarantee a correct response? Expected answer and boundary: No. Generation, interpretation and citation entailment can fail after retrieval succeeds. Visual purpose: show Query labels > Retrieved IDs | Claim > Exact source support. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. [Sources] https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401 ; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html. Original teaching example, not an empirical deployment claim. Cover artwork: /assets/week13/visual-provenance.json. Quantitative images: current week notebook execution record.
visual_purpose: Query labels > Retrieved IDs | Claim > Exact source support

title: Reciprocal rank rewards the first hit
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Reciprocal rank rewards the first hit. Define: For an answerable query, RR = 1/rank of the first relevant result. Walk through: [C,A,B] and [A,C,B] may have the same recall@3 but different reciprocal rank. Ask: Why report the rank convention? title: An evidence quote has a narrow role
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: An evidence quote has a narrow role. Define: An exact substring proves text location, not whether every derived claim follows. Walk through: Source: threshold 80 C. Claim: threshold 95 C. A correct source ID does not rescue the wrong number. Ask: What does automatic quote containment miss? Expected answer and boundary: It misses paraphrase meaning, omitted exceptions and contradictions. Human or task-specific semantic checks remain necessary. Visual purpose: show Citation ID > Quote containment > Meaning check > Bounded claim. title: Treat source instructions as data
notes: 2 minutes / practice. Teaching intent: Treat source instructions as data. Define: A malicious sentence in a passage cannot alter tool permissions. Walk through: The corpus includes an explicitly marked untrusted instruction. Retrieval may return it, but the workflow never executes it. Ask: Does a low similarity score secure a RAG system? Expected answer and boundary: No. Relevant malicious text can rank highly. Security enforcement must not depend on the retriever missing it. Visual purpose: show Retrieved text > Evidence boundary > No policy change. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation.
